correctness.rationale: For κ=λ/μ and ε=κ^(-1/2), standardized IG density ratio to φ is analytic uniformly on [-c,c] once εc<1; reflection z→−z exchanges ε→−ε, so its symmetric integral has only even Taylor orders. Independently expanded the logarithm and exponential through ε^6 with exact SymPy rationals, reproducing A2=(z^6−10z^4+15z^2)/8 and A4=z^12/384−3z^10/32+63z^8/64−105z^6/32+315z^4/128; checked differentiated Gaussian-polynomial primitives exactly. Integration gives c³(5−c²)φ(c)/4κ and −c⁵(c²−7)(c⁴−18c²+27)φ(c)/192κ², with analytic O_c(κ^−3). At c=√5 second coefficient = −19(√5)^5 φ(√5)/48; at c=1 it is 5φ(1)/16. These establish only fixed-radius eventual signs, not finite-κ uniform comparisons.
